Header: Puccinia graminis Agada wagi or wagi jirma

Prevention: When selecting varieties make sure they are suitable for the altitude where they will be grown
Avoid planting new wheat crop next to an infected field
Avoid walking through fields during the wet season to prevent disease spread from one plant to another
Rotate wheat with non-cereal crops: beans and other vegetables
Remove volunteer plants and alternative hosts (barberry and barley) before planting
Follow disease forecasting systems from national and international information centers
Prevent movement of infected plants across the field
Start working from the healthy part of the field before moving to the infected part
Monitoring: Start field observation 3-4 weeks after planting especially if the weather is warm and the humidity high
Inspect for orange pustules surrounded by a halo at the margin
Look for elongated reddish-brown pustules on stems and both sides of leaves
Pustules dislodge orange to blackish spores
Take action once a single pustule is observed
Direct Control: Remove and bury infected plant materials below 50 cm in the ground
Systemic fungicide used as foliar spray.
Spray at a rate of 0.5l/ha by dissolving in 200-250 l of water
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
A systemic curative and prrotectant triazole fungicide, FRAC group: 3
Toxic to aquatic organisms do not use near waterways.
No more than 2 applications per season.
Apply at a rate of 2.5-3.75 kg/ha.

Apply at first signs of the disease and again if infection occurs again.
